sap.m.sample.ComboBox2Columns.name: Combo box - Two columns layout
sap.m.sample.ComboBox2Columns.description: Use the combo box dropdown list with two columns layout if you need to display additional information to your options, like e.g. currencies to countries or abbreviations to systems.

sap.m.sample.ComboBoxClearIcon.name: ComboBox - Clear Icon
sap.m.sample.ComboBoxClearIcon.description: The combo box control can show 'clear' icon, which when pressed will remove the user's input and selected key.

sap.m.sample.ComboBoxDefaultFiltering.name: Combo box - Default Filtering
sap.m.sample.ComboBoxDefaultFiltering.description: The default filtering is 'starts with per term', which filters by the beginning of every word in every column. Autocomplete (type-ahead) works only for the first column, the leading value.

sap.m.sample.ComboBoxFilteringContains.name: Combo box - Custom filtering "Contains"
sap.m.sample.ComboBoxFilteringContains.description: You can override the default filtering "Starts with per term" with your own filter function using the setFilterFunction method. The "Contains" approach searches everywhere in the entries.

sap.m.sample.ComboBoxFilteringStartsWith.name: Combo box - Custom filtering "Starts with"
sap.m.sample.ComboBoxFilteringStartsWith.description: You can override the default filtering "Starts with per term" with your own filter function using the setFilterFunction method. The "Starts with" approach searches only in the beginning of the entries in both columns.

sap.m.sample.ComboBoxGrouping.name: ComboBox - Grouping of items

sap.m.sample.ComboBoxLazyLoading.name: Combo box - Deferred loading of the items
sap.m.sample.ComboBoxLazyLoading.description:
Use this feature to defer initialization of items until the point at which the items are needed. It can improve performance, reduce memory usage and unnecessary client/server round-trips.

Note: This feature loads the items once, it is not intended to be used for paging the results or loading more items on demand.

sap.m.sample.ComboBoxMaxPickerHeight.name: ComboBox - maxPickerHeight
sap.m.sample.ComboBoxMaxPickerHeight.description: Limit the picker popup height using maxPickerHeight property

sap.m.sample.ComboBoxSearchBoth.name: Combo box - Search in both columns
sap.m.sample.ComboBoxSearchBoth.description: Combo box dropdown list with search functionality which checks both columns. When you need to display additional information on your options, like e.g. keys of countries or system abbreviations, and want to search in those as well.

sap.m.sample.ComboBoxValidation.name: ComboBox - Validation
sap.m.sample.ComboBoxValidation.description: The combo box control could be restricted to allow selection only from the items in the list.

sap.m.sample.InitialPagePattern.name: InitialPage Pattern
sap.m.sample.InitialPagePattern.description:
The initial page floorplan allows the user to navigate to a single
object to view or edit it. The interaction point on the screen is a
single input field that relies on assisted input to direct the user to
the object in as few steps as possible (using features such as value
help and live search).

The floorplan is achieved with a single sap.uxap.ObjectPageLayout with
sap.uxap.ObjectPageDynamicHeaderTitle.

sap.m.Input is used as an Input within the Title.
sap.m.MessagePage is used as a section, which informs the user
if input is needed or if the searched value is not found.
sap.m.SelectDialog is used as a value help dialog for the input.

sap.m.sample.InputSuggestionsDynamic.name: Input - Suggestions - Dynamic
sap.m.sample.InputSuggestionsDynamic.description: With the Input control's suggest event, you can handle the suggestionItems yourself dynamically. sap.m.sample.InputSuggestionsOpenSearch.name: Input - Suggestions - OSP
sap.m.sample.InputSuggestionsOpenSearch.description: If you need to use an Open Search Provider (OSP) to supply possible values, you can do this with the Input control's suggest event, and build the suggestionItems dynamically according to the results of the Open Search call.

sap.m.sample.InputTypes.name: Input - Types
sap.m.sample.InputTypes.description: Input type corresponds to the type attribute of the HTML input tag. On touch devices, it controls the keyboard layout. On desktop, the effect of this setting is browser dependent.

sap.m.sample.InputValueState.name: Input - Value States
sap.m.sample.InputValueState.description: This example shows different input value states.

sap.m.sample.InputValueUpdate.description: Since 1.24 the value property of sap.m.Input is not updated on every keystroke, but first when the user presses Enter or leaves the input. sap.m.sample.LinkSubtle.name: Link - Subtle

sap.m.sample.ListActions.name: List - Custom Actions
sap.m.sample.ListActions.description: This example demonstrates how to add custom actions to list items. Dedicated 'Delete' and 'Edit' types can be used to add predefined actions to the list items. sap.m.sample.ListCounter.description: The counter of an item quickly shows how many detail entries are related, without having to navigate to the detail page.

sap.m.sample.ListDeletion.name: List - Deletion
sap.m.sample.ListDeletion.description: Setting 'Delete' mode on a List means you can trigger the deletion of single items with a single press. The application has to decide if an additional confirmation is required.

sap.m.sample.ListFooter.name: List - Footer
sap.m.sample.ListFooter.description: With the 'footerText' property you can set a message that is shown at the very end of the list.

sap.m.sample.ListGrouping.name: List - Grouping & Context Menu
sap.m.sample.ListGrouping.description: Grouping your items makes it easier for the user to browse and find the desired content. This example also shows the context menu for the items in the List control.

sap.m.sample.ListGrowing.name: List - Growing
sap.m.sample.ListGrowing.description: The Growing feature helps if your content is too big to be loaded/shown at once. It paginates the content into smaller chunks - aka pages - which are loaded/shown one after another. Random access to pages (e.g jumping to the end) is not possible. Depending on the model the content is loaded on demand (OData) or shown on demand (JSON).

sap.m.sample.ListItemTypes.name: List - Items Type
sap.m.sample.ListItemTypes.description: You can use the ‘type’ property of any list item, which inherits from ListItemBase control, to demonstrate all possible types (see sap.m.ListType). In this example, you can see the Standard List Item behavior when different values of ‘type’ property are selected.

sap.m.sample.ListLoading.name: List - Loading Indication
sap.m.sample.ListLoading.description: You can use enableBusyIndicator property to display loading animation while the data is being loaded from server. By default, this property is true and busy indicator will be shown after 1000ms. This behavior can be customized by setting the busyIndicatorDelay property. When this property is set to false, items stay on the List until data loading is completed.

sap.m.sample.ListNavType.name: List - Navigation Indication
sap.m.sample.ListNavType.description: If only a subset of the list items are navigable you should indicate those by setting their 'type' to 'Navigation'. This displays an navigation arrow. Do not show arrows if all items are navigable. This achieved by setting the 'type' to 'Active'.

sap.m.sample.ListNoData.name: List - No Data Indication
sap.m.sample.ListNoData.description: If the list is empty it indicates this state by displaying a message text.

sap.m.sample.ListSelection.name: List - Selection

sap.m.sample.ListSelectionSearch.name: List - Selection & Search
sap.m.sample.ListSelectionSearch.description: When searching a list with multi selection the previously selected items will stay selected. This is managed by the list control for you.

sap.m.sample.MultiInputWrapping.name: MultiInput - Suggestions wrapping
sap.m.sample.MultiInputWrapping.description: Suggestions wrap automatically when longer then the dropdown width

sap.m.sample.NavContainer.name: Nav Container
sap.m.sample.NavContainer.description: The Nav Container stacks multiple pages and offers an API to switch between them with some animation. Typically application developers would use the App control which inherits from NavContainer.

sap.m.sample.NewsContent.name: News Content
sap.m.sample.NewsContent.description: This control is used to display the news content text and subheader in a tile.

sap.m.sample.NotificationListGroup.name: Notification List Group
sap.m.sample.NotificationListGroup.description: A control suitable for grouping notifications.

sap.m.sample.NotificationListGroupBindin.name: Notification List Group with data bindings
sap.m.sample.NotificationListGroupBindin.description: A control suitable for grouping notifications. The sample uses JSON data bindings.

sap.m.sample.NotificationListGroupLazyLo.name: Notification List Group with lazy loading of the notifications
sap.m.sample.NotificationListGroupLazyLo.description: Notification List Group with lazy loading of the notifications.

sap.m.sample.NotificationListItem.name: Notification List Item
sap.m.sample.NotificationListItem.description: A list item suitable for showing notifications to the user.

sap.m.sample.NumericContentDifColors.name: Numeric Content of Different Colors
sap.m.sample.NumericContentDifColors.description: Shows NumericContent including numbers, units of measurement, and status arrows indicating a trend. The numbers can be colored according to their meaning.

sap.m.sample.NumericContentWithoutMargin.name: Numeric Content Without Margins
sap.m.sample.NumericContentWithoutMargin.description: This is an example of the NumericContent that contains no margins, so the control is aligned to the left and to the top without any margins.

sap.m.sample.NumericInput.name: Numeric Input
sap.m.sample.NumericInput.description: The NumericInput is a numeric input field that allows the user to enter or adjust a value using configurable step increments. It supports optional min/max bounds, decimal precision, and an optional description suffix for units or currencies.

sap.m.sample.NumericInputValueState.name: Numeric Input - Value States
sap.m.sample.NumericInputValueState.description: This example shows different NumericInput value states.

sap.m.sample.ObjectAttributeInTable.name: Object Attribute inside Table
sap.m.sample.ObjectAttributeInTable.description: This is an example of Object Attribute used inside Table.

sap.m.sample.ObjectAttributes.name: Object Attribute
sap.m.sample.ObjectAttributes.description: This is an example of Object Attribute used standalone.

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeader.name: Object Header
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeader.description: This is a Object Header which displays the basic information about objects similar to the Object List Item. Besides a title and number you can show multiple attributes (on the left) and statuses (on the right).

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderActiveAttribute.name: Object Header – Active Attributes
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderActiveAttribute.description: Active Object Attributes can trigger actions, such as navigating to related content inside or outside of the current application, or displaying additional information in a popover.

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderCircleImage.name: Object Header - with Circle-shaped Image
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderCircleImage.description:
An Object Header can set shape of the image by using 'imageShape' property. The shapes could be Square (by default) and Circle. 
Note: This example shows the image inside ObjectHeader with the responsive property set to true. On phone in portrait mode, the image is hidden.

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderCondensed.name: Object Header - Condensed
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderCondensed.description: The Object Header is shown in condensed mode with title, number, number unit and one attribute.

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderFavFlag.name: Object Header - Favorite & Flag
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderFavFlag.description:
The Object Header can indicate whether the object is a favorite, or has been flagged for further action. Changing these states is done elsewhere.

Note: The markFlagged and markFavorite properties are deprecated as of version 1.42. We recommend using the markers aggregation instead.

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderImage.name: Object Header - with Image
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderImage.description:
An Object Header will also make space for an image if one is specified, via a URL for the 'icon' property. 
Note: This example shows the image inside ObjectHeader with the responsive property set to false. On phone in portrait mode, the image remains visible.

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderMarkers.name: Object Header - markers aggregation
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderMarkers.description: This sample shows the different states of an Object Header, which can be set using the markers.

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderResponsiveI.name: Object Header Responsive I
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderResponsiveI.description: This is a responsive Object Header with a Title, 2 Statuses/Attributes rendered next to the title in a fullScreenOptimized mode (fullScreenOptimized = true).

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderResponsiveII.name: Object Header Responsive II
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderResponsiveII.description: This is a responsive Object Header with a Title, 2 Statuses/Attributes rendered below the title in a Master/Detail mode (fullScreenOptimized = false).

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderResponsiveIII.name: Object Header Responsive III
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderResponsiveIII.description: This is a responsive Object Header with a Title, number, 6 Statuses/Attributes rendered in 4 columns in a fullScreenOptimized mode (fullScreenOptimized = true).

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderResponsiveIV.name: Object Header Responsive IV
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderResponsiveIV.description: This is a responsive Object Header with a Title, number, 6 Statuses/Attributes rendered in 3 columns in a Master/Detail mode (fullScreenOptimized = false).

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderResponsiveV.name: Object Header Responsive V
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderResponsiveV.description: This is a responsive Object Header without a number and with a Title, 3 Statuses/Attributes.

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderTitleActive.name: Object Header - Active Title
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderTitleActive.description: The Object Header's title can be active to trigger further actions like showing additional information in a Popover.

sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderTitleSel.name: Object Header - Select Title
sap.m.sample.ObjectHeaderTitleSel.description: This is a Object Header with a title selection. This can be used to switch between variants of the business object being shown.

sap.m.sample.ObjectIdentifier.name: Object Identifier
sap.m.sample.ObjectIdentifier.description: The object identifier is a small building block representing an object by a title and short description. Often it is used in the first column of a table.

sap.m.sample.ObjectListItem.name: Object List Item
sap.m.sample.ObjectListItem.description: The Object List Item has many possibilities to provide a quick overview for an object within a list.

sap.m.sample.ObjectListItemMarkLocked.name: Object List Item - markLocked, markFlagged, markFavorite
sap.m.sample.ObjectListItemMarkLocked.description:
This sample shows the different states of an Object List Item, which can be set using the markLocked, markFlagged, and markFavorite properties.

Note: The markLocked, markFlagged, and markFavourite properties are deprecated as of version 1.42. We recommend using the markers aggregation instead.

sap.m.sample.ObjectListItemMarkers.name: Object List Item - markers aggregation
sap.m.sample.ObjectListItemMarkers.description: This sample shows the different states of an Object List Item, which can be set using the markers aggregation.

sap.m.sample.ObjectMarker.name: Object Marker in a table
sap.m.sample.ObjectMarker.description: The ObjectMarker is a small building block representing an object by an icon or text and icon. Often it is used in a table.

sap.m.sample.ObjectNumber.name: Object Number - Default Mode
sap.m.sample.ObjectNumber.description: The object number is a small building block representing an important, numerical attribute of an object together with it's unit. Often it is used in the last column of a table.

sap.m.sample.ObjectNumberCurrency.name: Object Number - Currency Mode
sap.m.sample.ObjectNumberCurrency.description: Shows ObjectNumber with displayMode Currency, demonstrating currency symbol vs ISO code rendering and decimal alignment across different currencies.

sap.m.sample.ObjectNumberUnit.name: Object Number - Unit Mode
sap.m.sample.ObjectNumberUnit.description: Shows ObjectNumber with displayMode Unit, demonstrating measurement values with localized unit labels and decimal alignment.

sap.m.sample.ObjectStatus.name: Object Status
sap.m.sample.ObjectStatus.description: The object status is a small building block representing a status with a semantic color.

sap.m.sample.OverflowToolbarDifferentCon.name: Overflow Toolbar - Different Controls
sap.m.sample.OverflowToolbarDifferentCon.description: Demonstrates different controls and their behavior when they are part of the OverflowToolbar.

sap.m.sample.OverflowToolbarFooter.name: Overflow Toolbar - in a table and in the footer of a page
sap.m.sample.OverflowToolbarFooter.description: Overflow Toolbar Button is useful for showing lists of action buttons that can display an icon in the toolbar, and icon+text when in the overflow.

sap.m.sample.OverflowToolbarSimple.name: Overflow Toolbar - layout
sap.m.sample.OverflowToolbarSimple.description: Overflow Toolbar can contain the same controls as Toolbar with the added benefit that buttons that do not fit are moved to an overflow area when overflow occurs.

sap.m.sample.PDFViewerEmbedded.name: PDF Viewer - Embedded
sap.m.sample.PDFViewerEmbedded.description: A PDF viewer embedded in another control.

sap.m.sample.PDFViewerMultiple.name: PDF Viewer - Two PDF Documents
sap.m.sample.PDFViewerMultiple.description: Two PDF viewer frames displayed side by side. The second frame has the property isTrustedSource set to false which opens the PDF viewer with the displayType set to Link

sap.m.sample.PDFViewerPopup.name: PDF Viewer - Popup
sap.m.sample.PDFViewerPopup.description: A PDF viewer opening as a popup dialog.

sap.m.sample.Page.name: Page,Toolbar and Bar
sap.m.sample.Page.description: Each screen of a mobile application is typically represented by a 'Page' consisting of a header, a scrollable content area and optionally a footer. The standard header offers a navigation button and a title. Alternatively you can provide a customer header. Gernerally you should use Toolbars in the Page. If you need a centered title you may use a Bar.

sap.m.sample.PageFloatingFooter.name: Page Floating Footer
sap.m.sample.PageFloatingFooter.description: The floating Footer allows the user to see the underlying content.

sap.m.sample.PageListReportIconTabBar.name: Flexible sizing - Icon Tab Bar
sap.m.sample.PageListReportIconTabBar.description: This page shows flexible sizing with an Icon Tab Bar: The upper part extends with its content, but doesn't react to viewport changes. The Icon Tab Bar reacts to the viewport size. The table inside takes the available space. If the minimum size of the table is reached, the page begins to scroll.

sap.m.sample.PageListReportToolbar.name: Flexible sizing - Toolbar
sap.m.sample.PageListReportToolbar.description: This page shows flexible sizing with a Toolbar. The upper part extends with its content, but doesn't react to viewport changes. The lower part reacts to the viewport size. The table inside takes the available space. If the minimum size of the table is reached, the page begins to scroll.

sap.m.sample.PageStandardClasses.name: Fiori Object Page - Standard Classes
sap.m.sample.PageStandardClasses.description: This page implements the same sample as in 'Fiori Sample Page - sapUiFioriObjectPage' using standard margin classes. In contrast to using 'sapUiFioriObjectPage', the margins used for form, list, table and panel are responsive: they adapt to the available screen width. For more information, please search for 'Standard Margins' and take a look at our samples.

sap.m.sample.Panel.name: Panel
sap.m.sample.Panel.description: Panels are helpful to group custom content. They can be decorated with header and info toolbars.

sap.m.sample.PanelBackgroundDesign.name: Panel - Background Design
sap.m.sample.PanelBackgroundDesign.description: Panels support different background designs for better visual distinction inside containers. [since rel. 1.150]

sap.m.sample.PanelExpanded.name: Panel - Expand / Collapse
sap.m.sample.PanelExpanded.description: Panels also have the possibility to expand/collapse their content (including the infoToolbar if available). [since rel. 1.22]

sap.m.sample.PanelSticky.name: Panel - Sticky header
sap.m.sample.PanelSticky.description: Panels can also have a sticky header. [since rel. 1.117]

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendar.name: simple Planning Calendar
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendar.description: PlanningCalendar with single row selection that illustrates the built-in views.

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarAppointment.name: Planning Calendar - with appointments in different sizes
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarAppointment.description: PlanningCalendar showing normal, half-sized and large appointments.

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarDnD.name: Planning Calendar - Drag and Drop
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarDnD.description: PlanningCalendar with draggable appointments. The sample represents three possible roles. If you are logged as an Admin, you can move appointments both within the same row and between different rows without any restrictions. As a Manager, you have the same rights as the Admin but appointments can be dropped only on free slots (no overlapping). As a team member you can only move the appointments within your own row. By pressing Ctrl/Cmd while dragging, the dropped appointment will copy the initial one.

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarMinMax.name: Planning Calendar - with min. and max. date
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarMinMax.description: PlanningCalendar with min. date 2000-01-01 and max. date 2050-12-31

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarModifyAppoi.name: Planning Calendar - with appointments modification
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarModifyAppoi.description: PlanningCalendar containing sap.m.Popover with information for the appointments and sap.m.Dialog for creating a new appointment. Note: Illustrates how the PlanningCalendar can be used in combination with the sap.m.Popover and sap.m.Dialog controls for details/create. These features are NOT part of the control.

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarMulti.name: Planning Calendar - multiple selection
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarMulti.description: PlanningCalendar with multiple row selection. No interval headers are displayed. On click on an interval a new appointment is created.

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarOneLine.name: Planning Calendar - with one line appointments and multiple appointments selection option
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarOneLine.description: PlanningCalendar showing appointment with only title in one line to save space. The interval headers are only shown if there are some assigned in the visible area.

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarRecurringIt.name: Planning Calendar - with Recurring Calendar Items

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarRelativeVie.name: Planning Calendar - with relative views
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarRelativeVie.description: PlanningCalendar with relative views. The relative periods are not directly related to dates, but periods with pre-defined duration.

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarSingle.name: Planning Calendar - without row header
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarSingle.description: PlanningCalendar with only one row without row header.  On click on an interval a new appointment is created.

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarViews.name: Planning Calendar - with custom views
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarViews.description: PlanningCalendar with custom views to set number of hours, days and months and change view description. It illustrates both built-in and custom views. Sub-intervals are shown. Custom non-working days and hours are set. In months view some appointments are grouped. The group appointment mode can be toggled to expand the appointments.

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarWeekNumberi.name: Planning Calendar - week numbering
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarWeekNumberi.description: Demonstrates PlanningCalendar with different week numbering (only Date Picker, 1 Week and 1 Month views are affected).

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarWithLegend.name: Planning Calendar - with legend and option to change the first day of week
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarWithLegend.description: PlanningCalendar inside the main part of a sap.ui.layout.DynamicSideContent and a sap.m.PlanningCalendarLegend inside the side part. The legend includes calendar and appointments sections. For each sap.m.PlanningCalendarRow in the sap.m.PlanningCalendar some specific special dates of type non-working are set.

sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarWithStickyH.name: Planning Calendar - with header that remains visible (fixed on top) on scroll
sap.m.sample.PlanningCalendarWithStickyH.description: PlanningCalendar with header area that remains visible (fixed on top) when the rest of the content is scrolled out of view.

sap.m.sample.Popover.name: Popover
sap.m.sample.Popover.description: The Popover controls allows to show contextual information without leaving the current page. Press somewhere outside the popover to close it.

sap.m.sample.PopoverControllingCloseBeha.name: Popover Controlling Closing Behavior
sap.m.sample.PopoverControllingCloseBeha.description: In some cases the closing behavior of the Popover can lead to drill down navigation. This sample demonstrates how you can control this. When the Popover is opened, add a style "pointer-events: none" to the area that should remain static and when the Popover is closed, remove it. Please note that, when having nested controls with "pointer-events" set, depending on the value of the property, internal controls may fire events, which will bubble up and trigger other events where applicable. The application needs to handle such cases.

sap.m.sample.PopoverNavCon.name: Popover with NavContainer
sap.m.sample.PopoverNavCon.description: You can nest NavContainers in Popovers (and Dialogs) to navigate to further details in place.

sap.m.sample.PopoverWithinArea.name: Popover in Custom Within Area
sap.m.sample.PopoverWithinArea.description: Within area of sap.ui.core.Popup determines where all popups (including popovers) are positioned.

sap.m.sample.ProgressIndicator.name: Progress Indicator
sap.m.sample.ProgressIndicator.description: Shows the progress of a process in a graphical way. To indicate the progress, the inside of the ProgressIndicator is filled with a color.

sap.m.sample.ProgressIndicatorWithAnnoun.name: Progress Indicator With Announcement
sap.m.sample.ProgressIndicatorWithAnnoun.description: Announce the progress of the ProgressIndicator.

sap.m.sample.PullToRefresh.name: Pull To Refresh
sap.m.sample.PullToRefresh.description: With the Pull to Refresh you can trigger an update operation by swiping the current page down on touch devices. On other devices the Pull To Refresh is visible all the time and the user clicks it like a button.

sap.m.sample.QuickViewAvatarConfiguratio.name: QuickView with Different Configurations of Avatar
sap.m.sample.QuickViewAvatarConfiguratio.description: QuickView with fallback icon, initials, display shape and other avatar properties.

sap.m.sample.QuickViewCardScrollBar.name: QuickViewCard Scroll Example
sap.m.sample.QuickViewCardScrollBar.description: QuickViewCard embedded in container with scroll bar

sap.m.sample.QuickViewNavOrigin.name: QuickView with Navigation and Data Binding
sap.m.sample.QuickViewNavOrigin.description: QuickView using navOrigin parameter when navigating.

sap.m.sample.RadioButton.name: Radio Button
sap.m.sample.RadioButton.description: Typically the Radio Button is used by other controls. E.g. the List uses it for the single selection. But you can also use the Radio Buttons control directly, to allow selection of exactly one of multiple options.

sap.m.sample.RadioButtonGroup.name: Radio Button Group
sap.m.sample.RadioButtonGroup.description: A wrapper for a group of radio buttons.

sap.m.sample.RangeSlider.name: RangeSlider
sap.m.sample.RangeSlider.description: With the RangeSlider a user can specify range from a numerical interval.

sap.m.sample.RatingIndicator.name: Rating Indicator
sap.m.sample.RatingIndicator.description: A Rating Indicator can be used to both indicate and/or rate content.

sap.m.sample.RefreshResponsive.name: Responsive Refresh
sap.m.sample.RefreshResponsive.description: An 'Responsive Refresh' can be achieved by the combination of a Search Field's refresh button and a Pull To Refresh, both of which appear depending on whether the device is touch-enabled. A growing stream of backend data is simulated here.

sap.m.sample.ResponsivePopover.name: Responsive Popover
sap.m.sample.ResponsivePopover.description: The Responsive Popover is an abstraction of Popover and Dialog. On the phone a Dialog will be shown. On tablet and desktop a Popover is shown.

sap.m.sample.ScrollContainer.name: Scroll Container
sap.m.sample.ScrollContainer.description: The Scroll Container is a control that can display arbitrary content within a limited screen area and provides touch scrolling to make all content accessible.

sap.m.sample.SearchField.name: Search Field
sap.m.sample.SearchField.description: Use the Search Field to let the user enter a search string and trigger the search process.

sap.m.sample.SearchFieldSuggestions.name: Search Field - Suggestions
sap.m.sample.SearchFieldSuggestions.description: Add suggestion capabilities to a basic Search Field.

sap.m.sample.SegmentedButton.name: Segmented Button
sap.m.sample.SegmentedButton.description: The Segmented Button allows the user to pick one out of many options for displaying the content of the current page. It is a UI pattern from iOS, now also available for other platforms. Putting the Segmented Button to a Bar control on non-iOS platforms will result in something very close to a tab.

sap.m.sample.SegmentedButtonDialog.name: Segmented Button in Dialog
sap.m.sample.SegmentedButtonDialog.description: Segmented Button used in Dialog component

sap.m.sample.SegmentedButtonLI.name: Segmented Button in Input List Item
sap.m.sample.SegmentedButtonLI.description: Segmented Button used in Input List Item component

sap.m.sample.SegmentedButtonVSD.name: Segmented Button in View Settings Dialog
sap.m.sample.SegmentedButtonVSD.description: Segmented Button used in View Settings Dialog component

sap.m.sample.Select.name: Select
sap.m.sample.Select.description: Illustrates the usage of a Select in header, footer and content of a page. Note the different display options.

sap.m.sample.Select2Columns.name: Select - Two columns layout
sap.m.sample.Select2Columns.description: Use the select dropdown list with two columns layout if you need to display additional information to your options, like e.g. currencies to countries or abbreviations to systems.

sap.m.sample.SelectChangeEvents.name: Select - Change Events
sap.m.sample.SelectChangeEvents.description: Demonstrates the use of 'change' and 'liveChange' events.

sap.m.sample.SelectDialog.name: Select Dialog
sap.m.sample.SelectDialog.description: The Select Dialog allows the user to search for and pick an item from a possibly long option list. Basically it is a convenience function to quickly assemble a Dialog, a Search Field and a List with Standard List Items. You can have single select or multi select mode. The dialog can remember the selections previously set on the dialog.

sap.m.sample.SelectDialogLazyLoading.name: Select Dialog Lazy Loading
sap.m.sample.SelectDialogLazyLoading.description: Select Dialog lazy loading example with JSON model.

sap.m.sample.SelectGrouping.name: Select - with grouped items
sap.m.sample.SelectGrouping.description: Illustrates the usage of a Select with items organized in groups using SeparatorItem as group headers.

sap.m.sample.SelectList.name: SelectList
sap.m.sample.SelectList.description: A SelectList allows the user to select one item from a list of choices.

sap.m.sample.SelectValueState.name: Select - Validation states
sap.m.sample.SelectValueState.description: Visualizes the validation state of the control, for example, Error, Warning and Success.

sap.m.sample.SelectWithIcons.name: Select - with icons
sap.m.sample.SelectWithIcons.description: Illustrates the usage of a Select with icons

sap.m.sample.SelectWithWrappedItemText.name: Select - Wrapping text
sap.m.sample.SelectWithWrappedItemText.description: Illustrates how the text in items wrap.

sap.m.sample.SemanticPageDraftIndicator.name: Semantic Page using Draft Indicator
sap.m.sample.SemanticPageDraftIndicator.description: Integration of Draft Indicator inside Semantic Page

sap.m.sample.SemanticPageFloatingFooter.name: Semantic Page using Floating Footer
sap.m.sample.SemanticPageFloatingFooter.description: Integration of Floating Footer inside Semantic Page

sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendar.name: Single Planning Calendar
sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendar.description: This sample demonstrates most of the features available for the SinglePlanningCalendar control.

sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarCreat.name: Single Planning Calendar - Create and Modify Appointments
sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarCreat.description: This sample demonstrates how the SinglePlanningCalendar control can be used in combination with sap.m.Dialog to create new appointments and sap.m.ResponsivePopover to edit already existing appointments. It also showcases how appointments can be deleted. Please note that these features are not part of the control.

sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarDND.name: Single Planning Calendar with Drag and Drop
sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarDND.description: SinglePlanningCalendar with enabled drag and drop functionality, allowing to create appointments with dragging and dropping, to change the start and end date of appointments by selecting and dragging their top or bottom end, and to copy and paste appointments.

sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarDateS.name: Single Planning Calendar with Multiple Date Selection
sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarDateS.description: SinglePlanningCalendar with multiple date selection functionality.

sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarRecur.name: Single Planning Calendar with Recurring Calendar Items

sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarSnapp.name: Single Planning Calendar with Snapping Header and option to change the first day of week
sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarSnapp.description: SinglePlanningCalendar showing the modes for snapping the header part of the calendar.

sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarWeekN.name: Single Planning Calendar - Week Numbering
sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarWeekN.description: This sample demonstrates how the SinglePlanningCalendar control can be used width different week numbering (only Week and Month views are affected)

sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarWithC.name: Single Planning Calendar with Custom Views
sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarWithC.description: SinglePlanningCalendar showing the provided predefined views and custom views.

sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarWithL.name: Single Planning Calendar with Legend and defined working hours
sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarWithL.description: SinglePlanningCalendar and PlanningCalendarLegend controls used as main and side parts of an sap.ui.layout.DynamicSideContent control. The calendar also shows the daily working hours.

sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarWithZ.name: Single Planning Calendar with Zoom In and Zoom Out behavior
sap.m.sample.SinglePlanningCalendarWithZ.description: SinglePlanningCalendar with enabled Zoom In and Zoom Out functionality.

sap.m.sample.SlideTile.name: Slide Tile
sap.m.sample.SlideTile.description: Shows Generic Tile with the 2x1 frame type displayed as sliding tiles.

sap.m.sample.Slider.name: Slider
sap.m.sample.Slider.description: With the Slider a user can choose a value from a numerical range.

sap.m.sample.SplitApp.name: SplitApp standard use case
sap.m.sample.SplitApp.description: The SplitApp is the base for each master detail application. It extends the sap.m.SplitContainer control.

sap.m.sample.SplitContainer.name: SplitContainer standard use case
sap.m.sample.SplitContainer.description: SplitContainer maintains two NavContainers if running on tablet or desktop and one NavContainer - on phone. The display of master NavContainer depends on the portrait/landscape orientation of the device and the mode of SplitContainer.

sap.m.sample.StandardListItem.name: Standard List Item
sap.m.sample.StandardListItem.description: This list item offers a standardized user interface for list content with only title.

sap.m.sample.StandardListItemAvatar.name: Standard List Item - Avatar
sap.m.sample.StandardListItemAvatar.description: This list item offers a standardized user interface for list content with title, description, and avatar.

sap.m.sample.StandardListItemDescription.name: Standard List Item - Description
sap.m.sample.StandardListItemDescription.description: This list item offers a standardized user interface for list content with title and description.

sap.m.sample.StandardListItemIcon.name: Standard List Item - Icon
sap.m.sample.StandardListItemIcon.description: This list item offers a standardized user interface for list content with title, description and icon.

sap.m.sample.StandardListItemInfo.name: Standard List Item - Info
sap.m.sample.StandardListItemInfo.description: This list item offers a standardized user interface for list content with title and info.

sap.m.sample.StandardListItemInfoStateIn.name: Standard List Item - Info State Inverted
sap.m.sample.StandardListItemInfoStateIn.description: This sample demonstrates the inverted rendering behavior of the info text and the info state of the StandardListItem control.

sap.m.sample.StandardListItemNavigated.name: Standard List Item - Navigated
sap.m.sample.StandardListItemNavigated.description: This example demonstrates the navigated property of the list item.

sap.m.sample.StandardListItemTitle.name: Standard List Item - Adapt Title
sap.m.sample.StandardListItemTitle.description: By default the title size adapts to the available space and gets bigger if the description is empty. List items with and without descriptions results in titles with different sizes. In this cases it is better to switch the size adaption off.

sap.m.sample.StandardListItemWrapping.name: Standard List Item - Wrapping
sap.m.sample.StandardListItemWrapping.description: This sample demonstrates the wrapping behavior of the title text and the description text. In desktop mode, the character limit is set to 300 characters, whereas in the phone mode, the character limit is set to 100 characters.

sap.m.sample.StandardMarginsAll.name: Margins All Around
sap.m.sample.StandardMarginsAll.description: Use standard margin classes 'sapUiTinyMargin', 'sapUiSmallMargin', 'sapUiMediumMargin' or 'sapUiLargeMargin' to add a 8px (0.5rem), 16px (1rem), 32px (2rem) or 48px (3rem) margin to your control. This will clear the area all around your control (outside its border).

sap.m.sample.StandardMarginsCollapse.name: Collapsing Margins
sap.m.sample.StandardMarginsCollapse.description: See how adjacent margins collapse to a single margin.

sap.m.sample.StandardMarginsEnforceWidth.name: Enforce Width 'auto'
sap.m.sample.StandardMarginsEnforceWidth.description: Some controls (for example the IconTabBar) do not have a 'width' property but still have a default width of 100%. We provide css class 'sapUiForceWidthAuto' to overwrite the control's width in such a case.

sap.m.sample.StandardMarginsResponsive.name: Responsive Margins
sap.m.sample.StandardMarginsResponsive.description: Clear the space around your control, where the margin depends on the device your are using.

sap.m.sample.StandardMarginsSingleSided.name: Single-Sided Margins
sap.m.sample.StandardMarginsSingleSided.description: Clear the space to the left, right, top or bottom of your control. Choose a size ('Tiny', 'Small', 'Medium' or 'Large', which stands for 8px (0.5rem), 16px (1rem), 32px (2rem) or 48px (3rem) respectively) and a direction ('Begin', 'End', 'Top' or 'Bottom', where 'Begin' is left and 'End' is right and vice versa in right-to-left mode). If you would like to clear a 32px space to the left (resp. right in rtl mode), you would add class 'sapUiMediumMarginBegin'. You may also add several classes which have to point to different directions though, for example you would add classes 'sapUiLargeMarginEnd sapUiLargeMarginBottom' to clear a 48px space to the bottom and to the right (resp. to the left in rtl mode).

sap.m.sample.StandardMarginsTwoSided.name: Two-Sided Margins
sap.m.sample.StandardMarginsTwoSided.description: Clear the space to the left and right, top and bottom of your control. Choose a size ('Tiny', 'Small', 'Medium' or 'Large', which stands for 8px (0.5rem), 16px (1rem), 32px (2rem) or 48px (3rem) respectively) and an orientation ('BeginEnd', 'TopBottom'). If you would like to clear a 32px space to the left and right, you would add class 'sapUiMediumMarginBeginEnd'.

sap.m.sample.StandardNegativeMarginsTwoS.name: Negative Margins
sap.m.sample.StandardNegativeMarginsTwoS.description: Use standard negative margin classes 'sapUiTinyNegativeMarginBeginEnd', 'sapUiSmallNegativeMarginBeginEnd', 'sapUiMediumNegativeMarginBeginEnd' or 'sapUiLargeNegativeMarginBeginEnd' to remove  0.5rem, 1rem, 2rem, or 3rem margin to the left and right edges of your control.

sap.m.sample.StandardNoMargins.name: Remove Margins
sap.m.sample.StandardNoMargins.description: Use our standard 'No-Margins' classes to remove existing margins from your control. You can either remove all margins at once or remove the margin on one or more sides.

sap.m.sample.StepInput.name: StepInput
sap.m.sample.StepInput.description: The StepInput allows the user to change stepwise a value by a predefined step and also to set additional description, such as units of measurement and currencies after the input field.

sap.m.sample.StepInputValueState.name: Step Input - Value States
sap.m.sample.StepInputValueState.description: This example shows different StepInput value states.

sap.m.sample.Switch.name: Switch
sap.m.sample.Switch.description: "Some say it is only a switch, I say it is one of the most stylish controls in the universe of mobile UI controls." (unknown developer)

sap.m.sample.TabContainer.name: Tab Container
sap.m.sample.TabContainer.description: The sap.m.TabContainer allows for working with multiple tabs.

sap.m.sample.TabContainerIcons.name: Tab Container - with icons and additional text
sap.m.sample.TabContainerIcons.description: This example shows how you can add additional text and an Icon to the tabs in TabContainer.

sap.m.sample.TabContainerMHC.name: Tab Container - Multi-instance handling concept
sap.m.sample.TabContainerMHC.description: Allows detail view / edit in sap.m.TabContainer after selecting items from table.

sap.m.sample.Table.name: Table - Columns
sap.m.sample.Table.description: The table shares many features with the list and, in addition, introduces columns. The table is fully responsive and can hide columns or shown them in-place if the screen space is not sufficient. This example also demonstrates the different table pop-in layout options along with sticky column headers, header toolbar and info toolbar options.

sap.m.sample.TableAlternateRowColors.name: Table - Alternate Row Colors
sap.m.sample.TableAlternateRowColors.description: Table with alternating light and dark background colors. Note: The effect of this feature is only visible in some themes (e.g. SAP Belize or SAP Quartz).

sap.m.sample.TableAutoPopin.name: Table - Auto popin of the table columns
sap.m.sample.TableAutoPopin.description: This example demonstrates the automatic pop-in behavior of the table and hiding columns instead of moving them into the pop-in depending on their importance.

sap.m.sample.TableBreadcrumb.name: Table - Breadcrumb
sap.m.sample.TableBreadcrumb.description: With an InfoToolbar and some crumb logic you can navigate simple hierarchies with a breadcrumb table approach.

sap.m.sample.TableColumnWidth.name: Table - Defining Column Width
sap.m.sample.TableColumnWidth.description: While defining the column width you can use percent values but you should be careful with them. Click to see some traps and tipps.

sap.m.sample.TableContextualWidthDynamic.name: Table - ContextualWidth (Dynamic)
sap.m.sample.TableContextualWidthDynamic.description: This example shows the container-based pop-in behavior. The container has dynamic width.

sap.m.sample.TableContextualWidthStatic.name: Table - ContextualWidth (Static)
sap.m.sample.TableContextualWidthStatic.description: This example shows the container-based pop-in behavior. The container has static width.

sap.m.sample.TableDnD.name: Table - Drag and Drop
sap.m.sample.TableDnD.description: Shows the different kinds of drag-and-drop capabilities across view boundaries along with custom context menu alternatives to perform these action.

sap.m.sample.TableIColumnHeaderMenu.name: Table - IColumnHeaderMenu
sap.m.sample.TableIColumnHeaderMenu.description: This example demonstrates an implementation of the IColumnHeaderMenu interface with the sap.m.Menu as a breakout scenario.

sap.m.sample.TableLayout.name: Table - Fixed vs Auto Layout
sap.m.sample.TableLayout.description:
You can use fixedLayout property to define the layout algorithm to be used for the table cells, rows, and columns.
When fixedLayout property is set to false, the width of the table and its cells depends on the content thereof. The column width is set by the widest unbreakable content in the cells.
By default, table is rendered with fixed layout algorithm. This means the horizontal layout only depends on the table's width and the width of the columns, not the contents of the cells. Cells in subsequent rows do not affect column widths.

sap.m.sample.TableMergeCells.name: Table - Merge Cells
sap.m.sample.TableMergeCells.description:
With column duplicate merging, you can improve the display of repeated data. See the effect of mergeDuplicates on the Supplier column, space permitting.
Note: This feature is ignored if a column is shown in the pop-in.

sap.m.sample.TableMultiSelectMode.name: Table - MultiSelectMode
sap.m.sample.TableMultiSelectMode.description: This example demonstrates the different multi-selection modes if the table is configured with MultiToggle mode and the sap.m.table.Title control.

sap.m.sample.TableNavigated.name: Table - Item Navigated
sap.m.sample.TableNavigated.description: This example demonstrates the navigated property of the item.

sap.m.sample.TableOutdated.name: Table - Outdated Data
sap.m.sample.TableOutdated.description: You can use the 'showOverlay' property to indicate that the table data is no longer up to date. When the user modifies the filter values of the table, this results in displaying an overlay, which disables operations on the table. Once the user chooses 'Filter', the filter values and table data are synchronized again and the overlay is removed.

sap.m.sample.TableScrollToIndex.name: Table - Scroll To Index
sap.m.sample.TableScrollToIndex.description: This sample demonstrates the scroll-to-index functionality.

sap.m.sample.TableSelectCopy.name: Table - CellSelector, CopyProvider
sap.m.sample.TableSelectCopy.description: This example demonstrates how the Table data can be copied to the clipboard via CopyProvider plugin.

sap.m.sample.TableSelectDialog.name: Table Select Dialog
sap.m.sample.TableSelectDialog.description: Similar to the Select Dialog, the Table Select Dialog presents selectable items in a table-based dialog, with filter functions. You can have single select or multi select mode. The dialog can remember the selections previously set on the dialog.

sap.m.sample.TableSelectDialogGrowing.name: Table Select Dialog Growing
sap.m.sample.TableSelectDialogGrowing.description: Table Select Dialog can be created with property growing set to true or false.

sap.m.sample.TableSticky.name: Table - Sticky
sap.m.sample.TableSticky.description: This example demonstrates the sticky behavior of the table header toolbar, info toolbar, column headers, and group headers.

sap.m.sample.TableStrictLayout.name: Table - Strict layout
sap.m.sample.TableStrictLayout.description: This example demonstrates the Strict layout and the column resizing of the table.

sap.m.sample.TableTest.name: Table Test with OPA
sap.m.sample.TableTest.description: The following example simulates a click on a list item in a table.

sap.m.sample.TableVerticalAlignment.name: Table - Vertical Alignment
sap.m.sample.TableVerticalAlignment.description: This is a good example of how to vertically align different elements within a Table's ColumnListItem row template.

sap.m.sample.TableViewSettingsDialog.name: Table - View Settings & Menus
sap.m.sample.TableViewSettingsDialog.description: The View Settings Dialog is standard UI pattern for specifying sorting, grouping and filtering. For a table it should be triggered by a button in the table header with the 'drop-down-list' icon. The active filter should be shown with the table's info bar. This example also shows the context menu for the items in the Table control.

sap.m.sample.Text.name: Text
sap.m.sample.Text.description: The text control can be used for embedding longer paragraphs of text into your application, that need text wrapping.

sap.m.sample.TextArea.name: Text Area
sap.m.sample.TextArea.description: The Text Area allows to enter multi-line text and automatically breaks to a new line for overflow text. If the text gets too big to be displayed at once the user can scroll up and down.

sap.m.sample.TextAreaGrowing.name: TextArea - Growing
sap.m.sample.TextAreaGrowing.description: Since 1.38 the growing property of sap.m.TextArea gives the ability of a control to automatically grow and shrink dynamically with its content.

sap.m.sample.TextAreaMaxLength.name: TextArea with MaxLength = true
sap.m.sample.TextAreaMaxLength.description: Shows the behavior of the control with the new showExceededText property (since 1.48) and maxLength = true

sap.m.sample.TextAreaValueStates.name: TextArea - Value States
sap.m.sample.TextAreaValueStates.description: This sample illustrates the different value states of the sap.m.TextArea control.

sap.m.sample.TextAreaValueUpdate.name: TextArea - Value Update
sap.m.sample.TextAreaValueUpdate.description: Since 1.30 the value property of sap.m.TextArea is not updated on every keystroke, but first when the user presses Enter or leaves the input. The change was necessary to fully support the standard UI5 data binding with formatters and types. If you still need immediate update you have 2 options: Handle liveChange events or enable the boolean property valueLiveUpdate.

sap.m.sample.TextEmptyIndicator.name: Text - Empty Indicator
sap.m.sample.TextEmptyIndicator.description: The Text control has a property allowing an empty text indicator to be displayed.

sap.m.sample.TextHyphenation.name: Text - Hyphenation
sap.m.sample.TextHyphenation.description: The Text control has a property allowing hyphenation.

sap.m.sample.TextMaxLines.name: Text - Max Lines
sap.m.sample.TextMaxLines.description: The Text control has a property to limit the number of lines for wrapping texts.

sap.m.sample.TextRenderWhitespace.name: Text - Render Whitespace
sap.m.sample.TextRenderWhitespace.description: The Text control has a property allowing browsers to render whitespace and tabs.

sap.m.sample.TileContainer.name: Tile Container
sap.m.sample.TileContainer.description: Tiles: a modern UI design pattern for overview & navigation.

sap.m.sample.TileContent.name: Tile Content

sap.m.sample.ToggleButton.description: Toggle Buttons can be toggled between pressed and normal state.

sap.m.sample.TokenizerMultiLine.description: Tokenizer with Multi-line support and Clear All button

sap.m.sample.ToolbarActive.description: Making an OverflowToolbar or a Toolbar active allows them to react to the click event.

sap.m.sample.ToolbarAlignment.name: OverflowToolbar - Alignment
sap.m.sample.ToolbarAlignment.description: OverflowToolbar and Toolbar are often used for left/right alignment. This is easily achieved with ToolbarSpacer.

sap.m.sample.ToolbarDesign.name: OverflowToolbar - Design and styling
sap.m.sample.ToolbarDesign.description: The Design and Style properties can be used to specify the visual design of the OverflowToolbar/Toolbar.

sap.m.sample.ToolbarEnabled.name: OverflowToolbar - Enabled
sap.m.sample.ToolbarEnabled.description: The Enabled property can be used to enable or disable all the controls inside the OverflowToolbar/Toolbar.

sap.m.sample.ToolbarResponsive.name: Toolbar - Responsive
sap.m.sample.ToolbarResponsive.description: Toolbar items can be displayed depending on the current device.

sap.m.sample.ToolbarShrinkable.name: Toolbar - Shrinkable items
sap.m.sample.ToolbarShrinkable.description: Toolbar items can shrink/expand when the toolbar is resized. This behavior is enabled/disabled via the ToolbarLayoutData layout. It is also possible to set min/max width for shrinkable items.

sap.m.sample.ToolbarVsBar.name: Toolbar vs Bar vs OverflowToolbar
sap.m.sample.ToolbarVsBar.description: Toolbar handles overflow by shrinking items. OverflowToolbar provides an overflow menu. Bar is able to perfectly center a text if nothing overflows.

sap.m.sample.Tree.name: Tree - Basic
sap.m.sample.Tree.description: Tree displays data in hierarchical structure.

sap.m.sample.TreeExpandMulti.name: Tree - Multi Expand & Collapse
sap.m.sample.TreeExpandMulti.description: This example shows how to expand/collapse multiple nodes and demonstrates the sticky header toolbar and info toolbar options.

sap.m.sample.TreeExpandTo.name: Tree - InitialExpand & CollapseAll
sap.m.sample.TreeExpandTo.description: This example shows the initial expand state and how to collapse all nodes.

sap.m.sample.TreeIcon.name: Tree - Icon & Context Menu
sap.m.sample.TreeIcon.description: Tree item with icon. This example also shows the context menu for the items in the Tree control.

sap.m.sample.TreeJSONLazyLoading.name: Tree - Lazy loading with a JSON model
sap.m.sample.TreeJSONLazyLoading.description: Shows how lazy loading with a JSON model can be done using the toggleOpenState event.

sap.m.sample.TreeOData.description: This example shows Tree with OData service.

sap.m.sample.TreeSelection.description: This example shows different selection modes of Tree.

sap.m.sample.TsHelloWorld.description: This sample demonstrates a TypeScript setup for developing UI5 applications.

sap.m.sample.UXCIntegration.description: This example illustrates the integration of UI5 Web Components into SAPUI5 applications.

sap.m.sample.UploadCollection.name: Upload Collection - Instant Upload
sap.m.sample.UploadCollection.description: This control allows you to upload single or multiple files from their devices (desktop, tablet or smartphone) and attach them to the application immediately. The selection and upload process is completed in one step and is automatically triggered by the UploadCollection control.

sap.m.sample.UploadCollectionFolderHiera.name: Upload Collection with Folder Hierarchy
sap.m.sample.UploadCollectionFolderHiera.description: Shows the UploadCollection with a navigable folder structure.

sap.m.sample.UploadCollectionForPendingU.name: Upload Collection - Upload Pending
sap.m.sample.UploadCollectionForPendingU.description: You can use this UploadCollection scenario to select single or mutliple files and to add them to the upload list first. In a second step, the application can upload the selected files by calling the upload() function.

sap.m.sample.UploadCollectionSortingFilt.name: With Grouping, Sorting and Filtering Feature
sap.m.sample.UploadCollectionSortingFilt.description: Shows the UploadCollection with grouping, sorting and filtering feature. After setting the criteria for filtering and sorting you get the filtering information displayed in the info toolbar.

sap.m.sample.UploadCollectionVersioning.name: With Download and Update Feature
sap.m.sample.UploadCollectionVersioning.description: Shows the UploadCollection with a download and update version feature. If one item is selected, you can download it or update the item to a new version. Both features can only be used in the Instant Upload scenario.

sap.m.sample.UploadSet.name: Upload Set
sap.m.sample.UploadSet.description: This sample shows an Upload Set control with a list of files to be uploaded and actions you can perform on them.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetCloudUpload.name: Upload Set - Upload files from cloud
sap.m.sample.UploadSetCloudUpload.description: Shows the UploadSet with the cloudFilePicker set as enabled. Now, files can be uploaded from cloud with the integrated cloudFilePicker control.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetCustomUploader.name: Upload Set with Custom Uploader
sap.m.sample.UploadSetCustomUploader.description: Shows how to customize the Upload Set control using a custom uploader.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetDirectoryUploads.name: Upload Set Directory Uploads
sap.m.sample.UploadSetDirectoryUploads.description: Shows the UploadSet with directory uploads enabled. Toolbar offer modes to switch between directory or file uploads.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetGroupingSortingFil.name: Upload Set with Grouping, Sorting and Filtering Feature
sap.m.sample.UploadSetGroupingSortingFil.description: Shows the UploadSet with grouping, sorting and filtering feature. After setting the criteria for filtering and sorting you get the filtering information displayed in the info toolbar.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTable.UploadSe.name: UploadSet With Table - File Preview
sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTable.UploadSe.description: This example showcases how uploaded files can be previewed with FilePreviewDialog control and its related configurations. UploadSetwithTable Control creates and use default instance of FilePreviewDialog, if not defined.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTable.UploadSe.name: UploadSet With Table - File uploads with user dialogs
sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTable.UploadSe.description: This example demonstrates usage of itemValidationHandler callback to leverage additional validations and configurations to the UploadSetwithTableitems, and also the manual trigger of the upload process. The user input can be captured for each file with the help of the user dialog implemented at the application controller, before its upload.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTable.UploadSe.name: UploadSet With Table - Growing & Selection modes
sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTable.UploadSe.description: The growing feature helps if the content is not being displayed at once. It paginates the content into smaller pages that are displayed one after another. Random access to the pages (e.g jumping to the end) is not possible. Depending on the model, the content is loaded on demand (OData) or it is shown on demand (JSON). This example also demonstrates modes of the control (e.g. None, SingleSelect, MultiSelect, Delete).

sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTable.UploadSe.name: UploadSet With Table - Personalization and Variant management
sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTable.UploadSe.description: This example showcases personalization and variant management for UploadSetwithTable.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Fi.name: Plugin for Responsive Table (sap.m.Table) - File Name validation configuration
sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Fi.description: This example demonstrates the usage of fileNameValidationConfig property to configure file name validation for renaming a file.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Fi.name: Plugin for Responsive Table (sap.m.Table) - File Preview with Custom Page Content for non supported file types
sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Fi.description: This example showcases how to display custom page content for non supported file types in the FilePreviewDialog control. The custom page content is displayed when the user tries to preview a file that is not supported by the FilePreviewDialog control. This sample demonstrates usage of customPageConentHandler property as a callback function to display custom page content.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Gr.name: Plugin for Grid Table (sap.ui.table.Table)
sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Gr.description: This example demonstrates the usage of UploadSetwithTable plugin for grid table with the features of upload, download, drag & drop, remove and rename of files. It also demonstrates how the uploaded files can be displayed in a table.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Mu.name: Plugin for Responsive Table (sap.m.Table) - Multiple plugin instances with multiple tables
sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Mu.description: This example demonstrates the usage of multiple plugin instances with multiple tables. The plugin instances are created for each table and the uploaded files are displayed in their respective tables.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Re.name: Plugin for Responsive Table (sap.m.Table) - File upload with user dialogs

sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Re.description: This example showcases how uploaded files can be previewed with FilePreviewDialog control and its related configuration. UploadSetwithTable plugin creates and uses default instance of FilePreviewDialog, if not defined.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Tr.name: Plugin for Tree Table (sap.ui.table.TreeTable)
sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Tr.description: This example demonstrates the usage of UploadSetwithTable plugin for tree table with the features of upload, download, drag & drop, remove and rename of files. It also demonstrates how the uploaded files can be displayed in a table.

sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Tr.name: Plugin for Tree Table with folder hierarchy & folder uploads
sap.m.sample.UploadSetwithTablePlugin.Tr.description: This example demonstrates the usage of UploadSetwithTable plugin with a tree table featuring folder hierarchy, folder creation, folder uploads, folder navigation with breadcrumbs and folder management

sap.ui.layout.sample.Form480.name: Fullscreen – address form with edit switch
sap.ui.layout.sample.Form480.description: A fullscreen address form with Edit / Save / Cancel in the page header, switching between a display and a change fragment; ResponsiveGridLayout arranges the columns.
sap.ui.layout.sample.Form480.why: docuindex.json has no entry for this id: the demo kit lists only the three variants (Form480_12120, _12120Dual, _Trial) as samples. The sample is real and self-contained, just undocumented upstream

sap.uxap.sample.ObjectPageXML.name: Object Page built entirely in XML
sap.uxap.sample.ObjectPageXML.description: An ObjectPageLayout declared in one XML view - header title, header content and five sections whose blocks come from four different block namespaces - rather than assembled in a controller.
sap.uxap.sample.ObjectPageXML.why: docuindex.json has no entry for this id (checked 2026-08-22 against the sap.uxap demokit index in an OpenUI5 checkout: 'ObjectPageXML' does not appear at all). The sample IS shipped - Component.js, manifest.json, controller/ and view/ are all there - but four of its five block types live in sap.uxap.testblocks.* and sap.uxap.sample.Headers.block, packages the demo kit does not publish as samples either, so the whole family is undocumented rather than this page alone
